# Independent audit: nonnilpotent sharp metabelian ribbon

**Verdict:** No mathematical or Lean scope blocker found. With H the pinned UT4(F11) witness on ports a,b, and J the checked affine semidirect product F7⋊C3, the subgroup S generated by x=(a,t), y=(b,l) has odd order, is metabelian, is not nilpotent, and its single-matching ribbon has a simple C32 and no simple C4, C8 or C16. This is sharp for the smallest **dyadic** cycle, not ordinary girth. No claim of the exact cardinality of S, minimal size, or coverage of the general Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture.

**Projection and cycle exclusion.** The left projection S→H maps x,y to the exact named ports and preserves signed rim moves and the spoke. The three base steps at each H neighbor set are injective, checked first at identity on both rims, then translated. Consequently if distinct neighbors of one actual vertex were sent to the same H vertex, their port indices would coincide and the actual neighbors would already coincide. This local property, not global injectivity or surjectivity onto H, is all the exclusion requires. A projected simple cycle can repeat globally but cannot immediately backtrack, also through the seam by cyclic indexing. The formal proof traces the first half forward and second half in reverse from the same start, shows no backtracking within either half, and separately checks that their first projected ports differ by local injection applied at the start. Their projected endpoints agree at the midpoint. Left translation brings the initial group element to one without changing the rim or any ports. At lengths 4, 8, 16, the imported exact endpoint checks prohibit intersection between half-walk endpoint sets for distinct first ports, establishing exclusions without assuming quotient simplicity.

**Group properties and scope.** In J, multiplication uses 2^i on F7; 2³=1 ensures the action is well-defined. The coordinate bijection gives exactly 21 elements, and the projections of x,y to J are t=(0,1), l=(1,0). The exact normal form l^(u.val)t^(i.val)=(u,i) proves the restricted projection onto J is surjective. The kernel of J→C3 consists of translations, so it is abelian and contains the derived subgroup. The checked identity [l⁻¹,t]=l≠1 keeps l in every term of the lower central series; the surjective map of each lower central term S→J proves nonnilpotence of S. The class-three H group is metabelian because its derived elements commute; projections and subgroup membership prove the analogous fact for S. Finite odd cardinality uses divisibility by the odd ambient product cardinal, not equality with that cardinal.

The graph on S is connected by generation: starting on the first rim, implement each x± letter on that rim, and each y± letter by a spoke, the appropriate move, and another spoke; take a final spoke to access the second rim. This is the paper consequence of the explicit generated-subgroup construction; connectivity is not a separate headline declaration in these three additions. The C32 itself follows from the imported all-finite-odd-metabelian theorem after the three exclusions, not from lifting an arbitrary 32-cycle in H. The local axiom logs for the exclusions, affine nonnilpotence, and final sharp statement report only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. I inspected sources and prior logs; I did not independently replay the full dependency bundle.
